text: Corpus [Lat.]: Ger. Körper ; Fr. corps ; Ital. corpo . Body or organ. Used in combination in many anatomical terms (e.g. corpus callosum ). See BRAIN (Glossary). Most American and many European neurologists drop the substantive in many such cases, and write e.g. callosum . Where various nouns are compounded with the same descriptive adjective (e.g. corpus fornicis as contrasted with crus fornicis ), corpus must be retained; but it should never be applied to replace 'nucleus' for an histological aggregate, as it properly refers to a part anatomically discrete. ( H.H. )
